context.title: When money comes in, Cover is repaid first, and people can't see the split
context.body: Cover gives KOHO members a zero-interest cash advance when their Spendable balance hits $0. It's repaid automatically: any money that comes in goes to Cover first, and only what's left reaches Spendable. That rule is fair and simple, but it happens out of sight. Cover no longer appears in the transaction feed, alerts show only the Spendable balance, and a small deposit can vanish into Cover entirely. People are left doing the maths themselves on payday, and some read the gap as an error.
assumptions: I haven't used KOHO myself. My view comes from KOHO's help centre and marketing pages, public reviews and complaints, and KOHO's own job posting, so the current app may already show more than I can see.
The next-deposit preview assumes KOHO can recognise a recurring direct deposit and estimate its amount from recent paycheques. I've shown it as an estimate ("about").
Amounts are illustrative: a $250 Cover limit with $150 used, a $1,240 paycheque and a $40 e-Transfer. I don't show the monthly Cover fee because it varies by limit.

KOHO has no public design system, so the prototype follows KOHO's own iOS screens on Mobbin: a white canvas, deep-purple pill buttons, the Spend / Credit / Borrow / Save segmented control, an image-backed Spendable card, outlined Add / Send / Cards chips, a lavender plan badge, uppercase section labels, bordered cards and the four-tab bar. I used Inter as a stand-in for KOHO's typeface, and a soft painted gradient instead of KOHO's artwork. There's no KOHO logo.
The split view was informed by Monarch's split-transaction screen, Ubank's split-income review and Stake's deposit detail with a plain-language status note, all on Mobbin.

goals.title: No surprises on payday
goals.body: Before money lands, show how much will go to Cover and how much will be left to spend.

goals.title: Every deposit explains itself
goals.body: When money comes in, show where it went, on the deposit itself, in plain language.

goals.title: Make the rule feel fair
goals.body: Turn "Cover is repaid first" from something you discover into something you expect, with your full limit visibly ready again.

jtbd: When my paycheque or a transfer comes in while I've been using Cover, I want to know how much will go to Cover and how much I can actually spend, so I can plan my week without doing the maths or worrying that something went wrong.

evidence.step: Money you add repays Cover first
evidence.finding: KOHO's help centre says money you add goes to your outstanding Cover balance first, and only the rest reaches Spendable. If a deposit is smaller than what you owe, the whole amount goes to Cover and nothing reaches Spendable.

source.label: KOHO Help: How does Cover (Cash Advance) work?

evidence.finding: A Cover update moved Cover out of the transaction feed: its balance now lives on the Cover page, and transaction alerts show only your Spendable balance. A $0.00 or negative Spendable is how you tell Cover paid for something.

source.label: KOHO Help: Cover updates, what you need to know

evidence.step: The split is explained with arithmetic
evidence.finding: KOHO's own help article spells out the split with a worked example: use $20 of Cover, add $50, and $20 goes to Cover while $30 stays in Spendable. People need it spelled out, and today that happens in a help article rather than on the deposit.

source.label: KOHO Help: If Cover spots me, how do I repay?

evidence.step: A cash-out read as an error
evidence.finding: In a July 2026 complaint, a member said $87.78 was withheld from a RoundUps cash-out because of a system error. KOHO replied that a negative Spendable balance had offset it, and that Cover is tracked separately from Spendable.

source.label: Better Business Bureau: KOHO Financial complaints

evidence.step: Cover is a core, growing product
evidence.finding: KOHO markets Cover as an overdraft alternative from $2 a month, with limits up to $500 and guaranteed approval. It's a product many members lean on between paycheques.
A September 2026 review of Cover notes a Reddit complaint after e-Transfers from Cover balances stopped, and says Cover-specific reviews are rare, so most feedback arrives through support.

approaches: Show where a deposit went, on the deposit itself
Preview the next deposit's split on Home before payday
Explain small deposits that go entirely to Cover
Let members choose how much of each deposit repays Cover
Alert members when Cover pays for a purchase, with what's left to repay

ranges.summary: Every incoming deposit shows a breakdown: how much repaid Cover, how much reached Spendable, and why.
pros: Answers "where did my money go?" in the place people look.

decision.title: Clear Payday: show the split before and after money lands
decision.body: Range 3. A next-deposit preview on Home, and a "where it went" breakdown on every deposit while Cover is in use, with a plain explanation of why.
reasons: The complaint above isn't about the rule, it's about not seeing it happen.
A preview alone breaks down on unexpected deposits; a breakdown alone still surprises people on payday.
Showing "your full $250 is ready again" turns repayment into a positive moment for Cover.
decision.tradeoff: The preview is an estimate. I'd label it clearly ("about", "based on your last 3 paycheques") and fall back to the exact breakdown once money lands.

depth.body: Built in KOHO's visual language. Switch between three moments: before payday, see a Cover chip with what's left to repay and a next-deposit card that splits about $1,240 into $150 for Cover and about $1,090 to spend. On payday, a toast says the paycheque arrived, Spendable updates and the deposit shows exactly where it went. With a small $40 top-up, the breakdown explains why all of it went to Cover and what's left. Motion is quick and purposeful (the split bar grows from Cover to Spendable, screens push like iOS), and turns gentler for people who reduce motion. Names and amounts are illustrative.

validation.method: I'd start with KOHO's support contacts and complaints that mention missing money, Cover or deposits, then run quick moderated tests with members who use Cover, around a real payday.
hypotheses: Members who see the split before payday contact support about "missing" money less often.
A breakdown on the deposit reduces disputes about money withheld from cash-outs and transfers.
Seeing "your full limit is ready again" increases how many members keep Cover after repaying.
